issues.body:

### Minecraft Version & Loader

1.21.1-NEOFORGE

### Issue

Unsure if I wanted to make a "Feature request" or report it as a bug.

Moonlight detects the Fabric API on Neoforge and rightfully sends out an error. [TxniLib](https://github.com/txnimc/TxniLib) is one library that includes **the entire Fabric API**, [as you have rightfully pointed out](https://github.com/txnimc/TxniLib/issues/12). However, the error in the logs does not directly mention TxniLib, instead just loosely mentioning the **Forgified Fabric API**, which makes tracking the culprit very difficult to the inexperienced developer.

### Logs & Media

It's really only this:
```
[22:07:21] [Render thread/ERROR] [Moonlight/]: Fabric API detected! This is not a Fabric mod, so please don't report related issues to MoonlightLib or its dependent(s). This can usually happen when using Connector, or when using a mod that does NOT have a native Neoforge implementation. This can easily lead to poor compatibility and other bizarre issues. Proceed at your own risk. 
 Mods that bundle Fabric API: [forgified-fabric-api-0.115.6+2.1.0+1.21.1.jar]
```

issues.title: [🐞]: Mixin collision on CartographyTableScreenMixin between Supplementaries and Moonlight
issues.body:
### Mandatory Troubleshooting

- [x] Use the LATEST version of the mod and ALL its dependencies (or ideally all your mods). Pro tip: don't install mods manually, use a launcher.
- [x] Don't use Optifine or hybrid servers (Mohist/Velocity/etc) and have tried without big game altering mods (Sodium/Lithium/etc).
- [x] Check that this bug hasn't been reported already.
- [x] Try with the mod alone. If issue does not persist then try removing half of your mods at the time to find the conflicting mod.

### Minecraft Version & Loader

1.21.1-NEOFORGE

### Issue

**Mod Version**: Supplementaries: [sua versão] / Moonlight Lib: [sua versão]

**Mod Loader**: NeoForge (Minecraft 1.21.1)

**Description**:
During launch or runtime mixin application on `CartographyTableScreen`, Moonlight's `containerTick` mixin fails to inject because Supplementaries has already applied a cancelling mixin to the same method target beforehand.

- **Technical Cause:** Supplementaries applies a mixin to `CartographyTableScreen.containerTick` that cancels or short-circuits method execution (`ci.cancel()`). When Moonlight attempts its own injection on `containerTick`, the target point is no longer reachable, causing the Mixin transformer to discard/skip Moonlight's injection.
- **Impact:** The game does **not** hard crash (gracefully caught/skipped by the Mixin transformer). However, dynamic interface updates or map preview features depending on Moonlight's cartography table tick mixin will fail to render or update properly.

**To Reproduce**:
1. Launch Minecraft 1.21.1 on NeoForge with Supplementaries and Moonlight Lib installed.
2. Load into a world and interact with a Cartography Table screen.
3. Check `latest.log` to observe the Mixin transformation cancellation warning/error for `CartographyTableScreenMixin` from Moonlight.

**Screenshots**:
N/A

**Additional context**:
- **Operating System**: CachyOS Linux
- **Java Version**: Java 21
- **Affected Target Class**: `net.minecraft.client.gui.screens.inventory.CartographyTableScreen`
- **Target Method**: `containerTick`
- It even happens in a clean instance with just the two of them together.

### Logs & Media

- Log: [latest.log](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/33397321/latest.log)

- Modlist: [Sandbox (C) - Modlist.html](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/33397332/Sandbox.C.-.Modlist.html)

issues.title: [1.20.1 Fabric] StackOverflowError when creating a new world - cyclic dependency involving "Moonlight Mods Dynamic Assets"
issues.body:
Body:
**Minecraft:** 1.20.1 (Fabric)
**Fabric Loader:** 0.19.5
**Moonlight:** 1.20-2.16.35 (fabric)

**Bug description:**
Clicking "Create New World" (also reproducible from the title screen) crashes the game with:
java.lang.StackOverflowError in the "mouseClicked event handler".

**Key stack frames (Yarn mappings):**
net.minecraft.class_8523 = DependencyTracker
method_51483 = containsReverseDependency

java.lang.StackOverflowError: mouseClicked event handler
    at net.minecraft.class_8523.method_51483 (DependencyTracker.containsReverseDependency)
    at net.minecraft.class_8523.method_51493
    ... (infinite mutual recursion, deepest into HashMultimap.get)

**Analysis:**
This is an infinite recursion in DependencyTracker.containsReverseDependency, i.e. a cyclic
dependency among the loaded data/resource packs, triggered when the pack dependency graph is
rebuilt (on world creation). I isolated it by binary-search removing mods one by one: the crash
still occurs with only the always-present packs left — "vanilla, fabric, Moonlight Mods Dynamic
Assets, KubeJS Resource Pack" — and removing KubeJS did not help either. This points to the
"Moonlight Mods Dynamic Assets" resource pack as the source of the cyclic dependency.

**Reproduction:**
1. Launch the modpack
2. From the title screen click Singleplayer / Create New World
3. Crash

**Crash report attached below (or provided on request).**

issues.title: [🐞]: Startup warning for Ars Elemental's Yellow Archwood: “Failed to find child … - log”
issues.body:
### Mandatory Troubleshooting

- [x] Use the LATEST version of the mod and ALL its dependencies (or ideally all your mods). Pro tip: don't install mods manually, use a launcher.
- [x] Don't use Optifine or hybrid servers (Mohist/Velocity/etc) and have tried without big game altering mods (Sodium/Lithium/etc).
- [x] Check that this bug hasn't been reported already.
- [ ] Try with the mod alone. If issue does not persist then try removing half of your mods at the time to find the conflicting mod.

### Minecraft Version & Loader

1.21.1-NEOFORGE

### Issue

### What happened?
The warning occurs with Moonlight Lib 3.5.2, the version bundled with ATM10 8.1. I also updated only Moonlight Lib to 3.6.4, leaving the other mods unchanged, and confirmed that the same warning still appears.
```
[modloading-sync-worker/WARN] [Moonlight/]: Failed to find child for WoodType: ars_elemental:yellow_archwood - log. Ignored! ERROR: No value present
```

I have also observed this warning with earlier versions.

For reference, the mod versions in my environment are:
- Minecraft: 1.21.1
- Ars Elemental: 0.7.10.1
- Moonlight Lib: 3.5.2 (bundled version) and 3.6.4 (manually updated)


### Testing scope
Both tests were performed in the modpack environment. I have not tested a minimal instance or performed a binary search through the installed mods, so I have left the corresponding troubleshooting checkbox unchecked.


### Suspected cause
The Yellow Archwood entry in HardcodedBlockTypes.java appears to associate its leaves with the following log identifier:

```java
leafReg.addSimpleFinder("ars_elemental", "yellow_archwood")
    .childBlock(LOG, ResourceLocation.parse("ars_nouveau:archwood_log"));
```


However, the Yellow Archwood blocks I verified in-game are:
```
ars_elemental:yellow_archwood_sapling
ars_elemental:yellow_archwood_leaves
ars_elemental:stripped_yellow_archwood_log
ars_elemental:stripped_yellow_archwood
ars_elemental:yellow_archwood_log
ars_elemental:yellow_archwood
```

The planks are shared with Ars Nouveau: ars_nouveau:archwood_planks. There is no separate Yellow Archwood plank variant in this setup.

Could the reference to `ars_nouveau:archwood_log` be causing the lookup failure? I have not tested a code change, so I am reporting this as a suspected cause rather than a confirmed fix.

I am not suggesting that Yellow Archwood should be registered as a separate plank type; the shared Archwood plank relationship may need to be preserved.

### Steps to reproduce
1. Install ATM10 version 8.1, which includes Moonlight Lib 3.5.2.
2. Launch the game and check the startup log for the warning quoted above.
3. Close the game and update only Moonlight Lib from 3.5.2 to 3.6.4, leaving the other mods unchanged.
4. Launch the game again and confirm that the same warning still appears.

These steps describe the modpack environment where I observed the issue; a minimal reproduction has not yet been tested.


### Logs & Media

Startup log with Moonlight Lib 3.5.2:
https://mclo.gs/xIPT8vR

issues.title: RegistryQueue.RegEntryHolder.initialize() is not re-entrancy-safe — a registry listener touching the value being registered recurses until StackOverflowError

labels.name: done
labels.description: fixed & it'll be in next version

issues.body:
## Summary

`RegEntryHolder.initialize()` guards on `this.holder != null`, but assigns
`this.holder` **after** `writableRegistry.register(...)` returns:

```java
void initialize(boolean throwMissingReg) {
    if (this.holder != null) return;                                  // (A) guard
    WritableRegistry writableRegistry = (WritableRegistry) BuiltInRegistries.REGISTRY.get(registryKey.location());
    if (writableRegistry == null) { ... }
    this.holder = writableRegistry.register(id, regSupplier.get(), RegistrationInfo.BUILT_IN);   // (B)
    ...
}
```

`register()` at (B) synchronously fires every registry-added listener. If any
listener reaches back into this same holder — directly or through the object being
registered — it re-enters `initialize()`, finds `holder` still `null` at (A),
calls `regSupplier.get()` again, and calls `register()` again. Unbounded
recursion, terminated only by `StackOverflowError`.

There is no in-progress flag and no "already present in the registry" check, so
guard (A) simply cannot fire during the window that (B) opens.

## Reproduction

Minecraft 1.21.1, Fabric Loader 0.19.3, dedicated server, **four mods**:

```
fabric-api-0.116.15+1.21.1.jar
moonlight-1.21.1-3.4.1-fabric.jar
spelunkery-1.21.1-0.4.3-fabric.jar
psychedelicraft-1.8.9+1.21.jar
```

`java -jar fabric-server-launch.jar nogui`. **12 boots out of 12 failed.** The
server never reaches "Done".

> Note for anyone reproducing: the real stack is swallowed by default. log4j's
> `ThrowableProxy` dies with `NoClassDefFoundError: Could not initialize class
> org.apache.logging.log4j.util.PrivateSecurityManagerStackTraceUtil` while
> rendering it, so `latest.log` shows only the log4j failure. Point
> `-Dlog4j.configurationFile` at a config whose layout uses `%ex` instead of
> `%xEx` and the trace appears.

## The cycle

```
Psychedelicraft  VanillaFluid.lambda$bootstrap$1(VanillaFluid.java:49)   RegistryEntryAddedCallback on Registries.FLUID
  -> VanillaFluid.register(VanillaFluid.java:57)                          calls toStill(value)
    -> VanillaFluid.toStill(VanillaFluid.java:79)                         ((FlowableFluid) fluid).getStill()
      -> Spelunkery SpringWater.getStill(SpringWater.java:56)             returns a Moonlight RegSupplier
        -> Moonlight RegEntryHolder.get(RegistryQueue.java:68)
          -> RegEntryHolder.comp_349(RegistryQueue.java:106)
            -> RegEntryHolder.initialize(RegistryQueue.java:89)           holder == null, so register()
              -> MappedRegistry.register(class_2370.java:163)
                -> fabric-registry-sync-v0 set handler (class_2370.java:1198)
                  -> RegistryEntryAddedCallback dispatch (class_2370.java:1153)
                    -> Psychedelicraft VanillaFluid.lambda$bootstrap$1(VanillaFluid.java:49)   <-- back to the top
```

…repeating until the stack is exhausted. The same `RegEntryHolder` instance is
re-entered every lap, and `holder` is still `null` on each one because the
assignment at (B) has not returned yet.

Immediately before the `StackOverflowError`, the log shows:

```
[main/INFO] (Psychedelicraft) Added vanilla fluid minecraft:water
[main/INFO] (Psychedelicraft) Added vanilla fluid minecraft:lava
[main/INFO] (Moonlight) Loaded config spelunkery-common.json
[main/INFO] (Psychedelicraft) Could not register vanilla fluid spelunkery:spring_water
java.lang.StackOverflowError
```

Psychedelicraft's `catch (Throwable e)` swallows the `StackOverflowError` and the
boot then collapses into a flood of `java.util.NoSuchElementException: No value
present` from the half-registered state; on a full pack this sometimes unwinds
without visible damage and sometimes leaves the holder unregistered, so
`Registries.freezeRegistries` throws `Some intrusive holders were not registered`.
That is why it looks intermittent: **the same mod set booted cleanly twice before
it first failed.**

## Suggested fix

An in-progress flag is enough:

```java
 void initialize(boolean throwMissingReg) {
     if (this.holder != null) return;
+    if (this.initializing) {
+        throw new IllegalStateException("Re-entrant initialization of " + this.id
+            + " - a registry listener accessed this entry while it was being registered");
+    }
+    this.initializing = true;
+    try {
         ...
         this.holder = writableRegistry.register(id, regSupplier.get(), RegistrationInfo.BUILT_IN);
         ...
+    } finally {
+        this.initializing = false;
+    }
 }
```

Throwing a clear `IllegalStateException` instead of recursing would already have
turned this from days of bisection into a one-line diagnosis. If you would rather
make it work than fail loudly, the alternative is to publish the holder before the
listeners run — e.g. consult `writableRegistry.getHolder(id)` on re-entry and
return that — but a fail-fast is the smaller and safer change.

## Whose bug is this

I looked at all three mods before filing here.

* **Spelunkery** does nothing unusual: `SpringWater.getStill()` returns
  `ModFluids.SPRING_WATER.get()`, the ordinary way to use a Moonlight
  `RegSupplier`.
* **Psychedelicraft** registers a `RegistryEntryAddedCallback` on
  `Registries.FLUID` and calls `((FlowableFluid) value).getStill()` from inside it
  (`VanillaFluid.java:44–57, 79`). That is an aggressive thing to do — calling
  arbitrary third-party code from inside a registry mutation — but it is a public
  Fabric API used as documented, and it is guarded with `try/catch`. A separate,
  friendlier report to Psychedelicraft asking them to defer that work out of the
  callback would be reasonable, but it would only paper over the cycle.
* **Moonlight** is the one holding a lazy-init invariant it does not enforce.
  Any listener on any registry can re-enter `initialize()`; fluids are just where
  it happened to show up first.

Happy to be told this belongs somewhere else.

## Confidence

Re-verified 2026-08-20 on Minecraft 1.21.1 with the four jars named above, all of
them the current release for 1.21.1 at the time of writing (Moonlight 3.4.1
2026-08-19, Spelunkery 0.4.3 2026-06-18). Reproduced 12/12; the stack above is
copied verbatim from the run. `initialize()` was read both from the `1.21` branch
source and disassembled out of the shipped `moonlight-1.21.1-3.4.1-fabric.jar`,
where the `putfield holder` is confirmed to sit after the `register` call and
there is no in-progress flag. Psychedelicraft's line numbers 49/57/79 match branch
`1.21` HEAD exactly. **Not checked:** whether the same re-entrancy is reachable on
NeoForge or on the `26.1.2` branch — I only tested Fabric 1.21.1 — and I did not
test the suggested patch.

issues.title: [🐞]: BlockBehavior Mixin performance issue
issues.body:
### Mandatory Troubleshooting

- [x] Use the LATEST version of the mod and ALL its dependencies (or ideally all your mods). Pro tip: don't install mods manually, use a launcher.
- [x] Don't use Optifine or hybrid servers (Mohist/Velocity/etc) and have tried without big game altering mods (Sodium/Lithium/etc).
- [x] Check that this bug hasn't been reported already.
- [x] Try with the mod alone. If issue does not persist then try removing half of your mods at the time to find the conflicting mod.

### Minecraft Version & Loader

1.21.1-NEOFORGE

### Issue

Injected at the tail of onRemove is this code in the BlockBehavior Mixin  
`if (state.is(newState.getBlock()) && !newState.hasBlockEntity()) {   
            level.removeBlockEntity(pos); //also needed here because previous check doesn't clear if its the same block  
}`  

While this works as intended, if the block is the same as the previous block and it is not a block entity, this has performance concerns, as level.removeBlockEntity pulls a chunk from the ServerChunkCache before it finds out there is no block entity, which can lead to a stalled thread during that time as seen in this spark profiler https://spark.lucko.me/9FJvRDRYi8

It should be sufficient to just check if the existing state has a block entity in the if statement as well to resolve this

issues.body:
Hi, I recently tried to build this project but Gradle wasn't able to find these 2 plugins:
* `net.mehvahdjukaar.candlelight`: Version 1.1.6 is not yet published. Latest one I can see is 1.1.5
* `com.possible-triangle`: Version 99.0 is not found. Only local builds get version 99.0.

I could workaround this by setting the versions manually and I think you should look into this.

issues.title: [Fabric 1.21.1] Repeated CLIENT_RESOURCES regeneration (moonlight:dynamic_resources) resetting resource packs and causing GUI crash
issues.body:
### BEFORE CONTINUING:

- [x] Always check you are using the latest version of these mods and its dependencies
- [x] Remove known problematic rendering mods such as Optifine, Sodium and others

### Version-Loader

1.21-fabric

### Moonlight Lib Version

moonlight-1.21-2.29.23-fabric

### Issue Detail



Minecraft: 1.21.1
Loader: Fabric
Moonlight version: latest (recently updated from 2.29.17)

I updated Moonlight from an older version (2.29.17) to a newer version recently and started experiencing the following issues.

Observed behavior:

- CLIENT_RESOURCES repeatedly regenerates.
- Logs repeatedly show Moonlight dynamic resource generation.
- Resource packs sometimes reset or reload unexpectedly.
- After this happens, interacting with GUI elements (for example clicking menu buttons or disconnecting from a server) may cause a crash.
- The crash occurs in Screen.mouseClicked with a NullPointerException.

Relevant log lines

Resource cache state for CLIENT_RESOURCES: needs regeneration
Starting runtime resource generation for pack type CLIENT_RESOURCES
Regenerating Dynamic CLIENT_RESOURCES Resources Provider [moonlight:dynamic_resources], requested by strategy REGEN_ON_EVERY_RELOAD

Crash location example:

mouseClicked event handler
net.minecraft.client.gui.screen.Screen.mouseClicked
NullPointerException

Important observation:

If Moonlight is removed from the modpack, all of the following problems disappear:

- Resource packs stop resetting
- CLIENT_RESOURCES regeneration stops repeating
- GUI crashes no longer occur

Before updating Moonlight, everything worked normally with the same modpack and resource packs.

issues.title: Proposal to organise the wood_set within ja_jp.json

labels.name: duplicate
labels.description: This issue or pull request already exists

issues.body:
This is not a bug report, but a straightforward question.
I am a Japanese translator, and I have some questions regarding how translation files are handled in series mods.

Among the series mods, my translations have been adopted for WoodGood and StoneZone.
However, it appears that the translation file for this mod also includes a translation for “wood_set” as seen in WoodGood.
The issue of duplicate “の” particles that I reported the other day also appears to stem from this cause.
Should wood_set be listed in the translation for this mod, or in the translation for WoodGood?

Additionally, regarding block_set, it appears that some translations are shared between WoodGood and StoneZone. (Example: `block_type.handcrafted.pillar_trim: %sの付柱`)
Given this, would it be appropriate to include these translations in Moonlight? Or would it be redundant and inappropriate?

I would appreciate your consideration.

issues.title: [🐞]: GUI item flickering when Gnetum is installed
issues.body:
### BEFORE CONTINUING:

- [x] Always check you are using the latest version of these mods and its dependencies
- [x] Remove known problematic rendering mods such as Optifine, Sodium and others

### Version-Loader

1.20.1-forge

### Moonlight Lib Version

moonlight-1.20-2.16.16

### Issue Detail

When Gnetum in installed, and hotbar contains a 3D item, items in GUIs flicker. Changing `consistent_entity_renderer_shading` from `NO_GUI` to either `FALSE` or `TRUE` resolves the flickering.

Gnetum is a mod that caches HUD elements to improve performance. If you disable the caching for hotbar in Gnetum's config, or if you have no 3D item in the hotbar, the flickering stops. Given this, we can picture a possible explanation for the issue:

<details>
<summary>(The explanation is incorrect, see linked PR instead)</summary>
- With Gnetum, hotbar is not rendered *every* frame, but maybe once in every 3 or 4 frames
- When it is rendered, Moonlight applies the shading fix to the 3D items in it
  - Then the GUI (screen) is rendered, but the shading fix is **not restored**
- When it is not rendered, no shading fix is applies
  - Then the GUI (screen) is rendered, and Moonlight does **not apply** the shading fix when it's set to `NO_GUI`

This is just a possible explanation I can think of. Please help me understand the issue so we can work on a solution together.
</details>

### Log Attachment

Not needed

3. Open JEI and see some blocks flicker (e.g. crafting table)
4. Remove the book from the hotbar, and see the blocks no longer flicker

labels.name: status: recalcitrant
labels.description: This will not be worked on or cannot solve

issues.body:
### BEFORE CONTINUING: - [x] Always check you are using the latest version of these mods and its dependencies - [x] Remove known problematic rendering mods such as Optifine, Sodium and others ### Version-Loader 1.20.1-FORGE ### Moonlight Lib Version moonlight-1.20-2.16.15-forge.jar ### Describe the Issue I noticed this issue when updating my moonlight version from moonlight-1.20-2.14.?? to the current version in my modpack. It caused some of the every compat supported 'coffee tables' and 'tables' (from unusual furniture) to disappear from my world, and from my creative menu. I decided to test this again in a different instance with ONLY the following mods installed: Ecologics vers: 2.2.2 Every Compat (wood is good) vers: 2.9.8 Framework vers: 0.7.15 JEI vers: 15.20.0.112 moonlight vers: 2.16.15 mrcrayfish furniture mod refurbished vers: 1.0.20 Unusual Furniture: 1.1.1 Forge Version: 47.4.0 The issue still persisted. If searching "Azalea", you will see that 'flowering azalea' wood has the 'table', and 'coffee table' missing from the creative menu. The regular azalea still has these items. I know flowering azalea wasn't the only texture to go missing, but it is the one I remember. Though it seemed to be only the coffee tables and tables that went missing. I haven't noticed others that went missing, though it is worth a check to see if others could be missing. It happened ONLY after updating moonlight (i did update 'wood is good' after), but i did testing and figured out it happened only after updating moonlight, NOT the 'every compat - wood is good' mod. It seems like the items are completely erased from the game as they disappeared from my world too after moonlight was updated. ### Log Attachment This log is from the smaller instance of the game. [latest.log](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/23106615/latest.log) ### OPTIONAL: To Produce 1) load the following mods and forge version together on minecraft 1.20.1: Ecologics vers: 2.2.2 Every Compat (wood is good) vers: 2.9.8 Framework vers: 0.7.15 JEI vers: 15.20.0.112 moonlight vers: 2.16.15 mrcrayfish furniture mod refurbished vers: 1.0.20 Unusual Furniture: 1.1.1 2) create a world 3) open the creative menu, or JEI, and search 'azalea' to see the comparison between 'flowering azalea wood', and 'azalea' wood where one has the tables and coffee tables, and one doesn't (flowering azalea). This is about it. Screenshots (if they load) shows where one has the tables, and the other doesn't.
Images
### OPTIONAL: Which mods are affected? Every Compat - Wood Is Good Ecologics Moonlight Library Unusual Furniture (possibly other furniture mods, and other mods that add in supported wood variants) These are just the mods I noticed. Thank you for your work on these awesome mods anyways! Hopefully this issue is an easy fix!

Wanted to reopen [811](https://github.com/MehVahdJukaar/WoodGood/issues/811), but I don't have permissions.

I reported an issue with this mod some time ago where it's leaves would not decay and it still seems to be a problem. Here's the list of all leaf blocks from this mod:

```
mysticsbiomes:strawberry_blossoms

and here's what manages to generate when I have Quark and Immersive Weathering installed:
```

on top of that, even these four carpets that manage to generate don't behave like other do - leaving leaf piles when the tree is cut down and it's leaves despawn. However, I'm not sure where this issue stems from - might be a problem between IW and Mystics Biomes.

issues.title: It would be nice if you could get the wood type of a Wood Log.
issues.body:
I am a mod developer on Fabric/1.20.1 and I use moonlight lib as a dependency. The `WoodTypeRegistry` and `WoodType.getChildren` letting me go from plank to slab/fence/etc. with cross mod compatibility is fantastic :)

For reference, my mod will "break down" blocks, e.g. on use of a tool, go from oak logs -> stripped -> planks  slabs -> fences -> sticks.

Unfortunately, I cannot find a nice way to go from a wood log to the wood type, i.e.

```java
woodRegistry.detectTypeFromBlock(Blocks.OAK_LOG, Registries.BLOCK.getId(Blocks.OAK_LOG))
```

Is empty since it only triggers for the planks.

Personally, I'll likely have to decipher the name of the block, and then try to find it in the `WoodTypeRegistry.getTypes()` entries. (Open to ideas).

So, I open this issue as a suggestion - it would be nice if Moonlight provided a function which, if given a Log/Stripped/hyphae `Block` and/or `Identifier` for said block, would give out the wood type, so you can figure out which planks are supposed to match it.

issues.body: Hi, So I noticed some items in JEI are missing, the items are still in the game and you can still craft them but they just aren't showing up when searched or in the creative menu. I did test all of these mods on their own and the items were in the game so I'm not sure how to fix it or what caused the items to disappear in the first place. Since I cant update the supplementary mods and EC without updating Create or the modpack crashes.

### Describe the Issue

Hello! I’m playing Minecraft 1.20.1 (Forge 47.3.0) with the Better Villagers mod. Every time I get near a desert village, my game crashes and I get a NoClassDefFoundError: net/irisshaders/iris/Iris in the logs.

From what I can gather, there seems to be a conflict between Moonlight Library (which many village-related mods use), Oculus (the Forge equivalent of Iris Shaders), and possibly “Better Villagers,” because the crash only happens when the desert village is being rendered or generated.

Snippet from the crash report:

    at net.mehvahdjukaar.moonlight.api.integration.IrisCompat.isIrisShaderFuckerActive(IrisCompat.java:10)
    ...
    
(Full crash report attached)

Versions
Minecraft: 1.20.1
Forge: 47.3.0
Better Villagers: 3.2.0 ((installed on both server and client)
Moonlight: 2.13.33 (installed on both server and client)
Oculus: 1.6.15a (client side only)
I’m hosting a small server on my own PC, and the server itself never crashes—only my client crashes (I get disconnected) whenever I approach a desert village. Other village types seem unaffected.

Any suggestions or fixes would be greatly appreciated!

issues.title: [🐞]: Generation of dynamic resources for foreign namespaces doesn't work out of the box
[🐞]: Dynamic fluid tags get generated under `tags/fluid` instead of `tags/fluids`
issues.body:
### BEFORE CONTINUING:

- [X] Always check you are using the latest version of these mods and its dependencies
- [X] Remove known problematic rendering mods such as Optifine, Sodium and others

### Version-Loader

1.20.1-fabric

### Moonlight Lib Version

moonlight 1.20-2.8.57

### Issue Detail

I tried using a `DynServerResourcesGenerator` to dynamically add tags to my mod's fluids, using `dynamicPack#addTag`. When it looked like the tags hadn't been registered in-game, I went to look at the code: 
```java
public void addTag(SimpleTagBuilder builder, RegistryKey<?> type) {
        Identifier tagId = builder.getId();
        String tagPath = type.getValue().getPath();
        if (tagPath.equals("block") || tagPath.equals("entity_type") || tagPath.equals("item")) {
            tagPath = tagPath + "s";
        }
        // ...
```
The if statement tries pluralizing the tag folders when needed, but it misses fluids, which are saved under `tags/fluids`. The debug resource dump shows that the dynamic tags do indeed get saved under the incorrect `tags/fluid`.

1) Use `DynamicDataPack#addTag` to add a fluid tag, and implement any distinctive functionality based on it.

3) Check the debug resource dump to find the tags are generated under `tags/fluid` instead of `tags/fluids`.

issues.title: Model JSONs being cleared after resource pack reload
issues.body:
Hi there, a player reported issues with hanging signs' item models not working when they enable the dynamic resources optimization in ModernFix. This patch causes models to load on the fly in-game instead of them all being loaded at once during resource pack reloads. After some digging I found that this issue was introduced by https://github.com/MehVahdJukaar/Moonlight/commit/19559dde5e6e217083ab9cf4d2b1cc83d18e94fd as the model JSONs are now cleared from memory as soon as resource pack reloading finishes. Downgrading to Moonlight 2.2.37 fixed the issue (I was testing on 1.19.2, not sure if this applies elsewhere). 

Is it possible to mark blockstates & model JSONs as persistent so they don't get cleared, or store the data on disk so that it can be reloaded if necessary? I would hope the JSONs alone are not too large unless there are thousands of them.

issues.title: [1.19.2] 16th of May update broke things in an odd way
issues.body:
I opened CurseForge launcher today to my normal 1.19.2 modpack (in which, thus far, I've been keeping all mods up to date) to see that I had 34 mods pending an update. Irresponsibly and stupidly, I clicked "update all," hoping all would work out fine. My game proceeded to crash on launch, experiencing an infinite Mojang loading screen, with brief glimpses of Not Enough Crashes flashing beneath, with every single character nothing but unicode squares. Going into each mod that I just "updated" it was revealed that CurseForge actually downdated (de-updated) all 34 affected mods to versions hovering around mid-to-late 2022, most around August to October. The modpack was only created around April 28th. I've now reverted everything and the pack seems to be working again. This mod was the only one to release a new version today so it leads me to believe it may somehow be the cause.
Here is a list of the affected mods, all of which were downdated:
``` Additional Additions AttributeFix Botany Trees Bottle Your XP Clear Despawn Comforts Convenient Name Tags Creeper Overhaul Easy Magic Expert Armor Explorer's Compass Falling Leaves FallingTree Friends & Foes (but neither of it's optional tweak mods) Galosphere Harvest with Ease Infinity Buttons Lithium More Axolotl Variants Mod Macaw's Lights and Lamps Mystical Oak Tree Not Enough Animations Nutritious Milk Raised Resource Pack Overrides Sound Physics Remastered Supplementaries Squared (but not base Supplementaries) Transparent UnionLib Visuality Zombies Villagers from Spawner Zoomify ```

issues.title: CME Race condition when launching the game

labels.name: done
labels.description: fixed & it'll be in next version

issues.body:
I am reporting this here as I am fairly certain it is on Moonlight's end and not JAOPCA. But recently after installing both Harvest Season and Immersive Weathering (I already had Supplementaries installed), I started getting sporadic CME's when launching Minecraft (sometimes it launches and other times it fails).

Crash Report: https://gist.github.com/pupnewfster/b618a23b041f2c352c275067a6855be2

It seems to reference [this](https://github.com/TheLMiffy1111/JAOPCA/blob/f73d91c2658b36345fb1dad527d816d3ba2c8f03/src/main/java/thelm/jaopca/data/DataCollector.java#L89) line in JAOPCA that just creates a new instance of vanilla's `MultiPackResourceManager`, and I suspect the issue is that given JAOPCA does this during mod construction (which is parallel on forge) it is possible that your mixin is iterating its list of listeners at the same time that other mods using this lib are being constructed and added to your internal list of listeners.

Versions:
Forge: 43.1.47
JAOPCA: 4.2.1.2
Moonlight: 2.1.4
Supplemetaries: 2.2.13
Harvest Season: 1.0.3
Immersive Weathering: 1.1.4

issues.title: Crash with WilderWild and BetterX
issues.body:
**MC** 1.19.2
**[QSL](https://modrinth.com/mod/qsl)** 4.0.0 beta 9
**[WilderWild](https://modrinth.com/mod/wilder-wild)** 1.0.5
**Moonlight Lib** 2.0.17 (it's not needed for any of the mods, only to reproduce the crash; I personally need it for Supplementaries which doesn't have to be installed to reproduce the crash)
**[BCLib](https://www.curseforge.com/minecraft/mc-mods/bclib)** 2.1.0
**[BetterEnd](https://www.curseforge.com/minecraft/mc-mods/betterend)** 2.1.0
**[BetterNether](https://www.curseforge.com/minecraft/mc-mods/betternether)** 7.1.0

To reproduce:

1. Install WilderWild, Moonlight and BCLib
2. Install either BetterEnd or BetterNether (or both, in which case BetterNether will be blamed for the crash)
3. Launch the game and crash

BetterX mods don't seem to be incompatible with WilderWild on their own, but only with Moonlight present.

Removing either WilderWild, Moonlight Lib or both BetterX mods lets the game start normally. Initially reported to WilderWild here: https://github.com/Soro335/WilderWild/issues/85. Since then every mod on the list has been updated, but the crash is still reproducible. I updated the logs to reflect that.

Logs include latest.log and crash log for the BetterEnd crash, but only the latest.log for BetterNether, because it does not generate a crash log: https://gist.github.com/Footage2-Amply-Pounce/e7506db63847f6f7f315af3cddee93c6

issues.title: Vivecraft compatibility
issues.body: Hi, I'm one of the Vivecraft devs. Your mod currently crashes when loaded with Vivecraft, due to this mixin failing as it conflicts with one of our patches: https://github.com/MehVahdJukaar/Selene/blob/master/src/main/java/net/mehvahdjukaar/selene/mixins/FirstPersonRendererMixin.java Since it appears to just be a handler for first person animations, which I don't think would look right in VR anyways, it'd probably be fine to just disable it when Vivecraft is detected or otherwise have the mixin not crash the game when it fails.

issues.title: Soft Fluid handling adds empty Compound NBT tag to Forge fluids that had null NBT.
issues.body:
When you e.g. use a Supplementaries faucet to put a fluid that does not have NBT in a Forge fluid handler, it will put an empty NBT tag rather than null, which will cause it not to be considered equal to the original fluid by most mods.

I believe this issue is caused by the use of getOrCreateTag in https://github.com/MehVahdJukaar/Selene/blob/HEAD/src/main/java/net/mehvahdjukaar/selene/fluids/SoftFluidHolder.java#L559 .
